recipes.title: 72-Hour Pizza Dough
recipes.yield: three ~318 g balls (12 to 13 inch pies) or two ~477 g balls

groups.name: Final dough
ingredients: 270 g water (250 g up front, 20 g held for bassinage)

steps: Day 1, ~9pm: disperse the 0.15 g yeast in the 80 g water, then stir in the 80 g flour.
Mix 5 g mother with 30 g flour and 30 g water to a paste.
Leave both at ~70F for 12 hours.
Day 2, ~9am: check the levain is roughly doubled and a spoonful floats; give it 2 to 3 more hours if not.
Mix the 470 g flour, malt and 0.15 g yeast in a large bowl.
Add 250 g water and 30 g levain to the poolish and stir to loosen.
Combine wet into dry and mix about 3 minutes until no dry flour remains.
Cover and rest 1 hour.
Add the salt and the reserved 20 g water; squeeze and fold about 1 minute until absorbed.
Work in the olive oil until it disappears.
Rest 1 hour at 70 to 75F.
Check dough temperature: target 70 to 75F.
Divide into three ~318 g pieces (or two ~477 g).
Ball each tightly with a sealed seam.
Place each in a lightly oiled 2-qt round container and lid.
Rest 30 minutes at room temperature, then refrigerate at 36 to 40F for 72 to 96 hours.
Bake day: pull the containers 2 to 3 hours ahead to come fully to room temperature.
Preheat the steel 6 to 8 inches below the broiler at 550F for 60 minutes; switch to broil for the last 10 minutes.
Shape by hand from the center out, leaving a 1-inch rim. No rolling pin.
Launch from a semolina-dusted wood peel, dressing in under 60 seconds.
Bake 5 to 7 minutes, rotating halfway.
recipes.notes: Past 96 hours the dough goes slack. Refresh the mother (20 g mother, 40 g flour, 20 g water) in the same session as the levain build.

nutrition.serving: one dough ball, about 318 g (1 of 3)
nutrition.assumptions: Dough only: 30 g levain taken as half flour and half water; container oil, semolina and toppings left out.

recipes.title: Apple Cider Doughnut Focaccia

groups.name: Cinnamon sugar
ingredients: 8 g cinnamon sticks, ground (about 3 to 4 sticks)

groups.name: Dough
ingredients: 200 g sourdough discard, 100% hydration, cold and unfed is fine

groups.name: To bake and finish
ingredients: 30 g olive oil, for the pan

steps: Warm the cinnamon sticks in a dry skillet over medium heat, 1 to 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Cool, break up and grind the cinnamon in a spice grinder. Sift.
Mix the ground cinnamon with the sugar and 1 g salt. Store airtight.
Mix the flour, discard, water, cider reduction, 12 g salt, yeast, ground cinnamon and 40 g olive oil until no dry flour remains.
With a wet hand, lift and fold the dough over itself 4 times, rotating the bowl.
Repeat the folds 3 more times at 30 minute intervals.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, 12 to 24 hours, toward the back of the fridge.
Pour 30 g olive oil into the pan, transfer the dough and turn to coat.
Proof at room temperature until puffy and relaxed to the edges, 2 to 3 hours.
Heat the oven to 425F.
Dimple the dough to the bottom of the pan with oiled fingers.
Bake 22 to 28 minutes, until deep golden and pulling from the sides.
Turn out, brush all over with the melted butter and press the top and sides into the cinnamon sugar.
recipes.notes: Serve with the [cider cream cheese glaze](cider-cream-cheese-glaze) for dipping. For a 36 hour cold ferment, use 2 g yeast instead of 3 g.

nutrition.assumptions: Cut into 12 pieces; all of the cinnamon sugar and pan oil assumed to end up on the bread, and the optional 4 g dough cinnamon is included. Glaze not included.

ingredients: 1130 g beef chuck roast, cut into large chunks (about 2.5 lb)
30 g garlic, peeled, left whole (about 6 cloves)

steps: Toast the guajillo, ancho and morita in a dry pan over medium, 20 to 30 seconds a side, with the vent running.
Soak the toasted chiles in hot water 20 minutes.
Blend the soaked chiles with the chipotles, adobo, onion, garlic, broth, vinegar, cumin, oregano, salt and MSG until smooth.
Sear the chuck hard in a skillet.
Deglaze the skillet into the crockpot.
Add the beef, sauce and bay leaves to the crockpot.

Lift the meat out with a slotted spoon.
Skim the fat from the liquid and pull the bay leaves.
Reduce the liquid hard in a wide saucepan, 15 minutes or more, until it coats a spoon and a finger track across the back holds.
Taste the reduced sauce for salt.
Shred the meat and toss with enough sauce to coat; reserve any extra sauce.
recipes.notes: Reduce the liquid well before tossing; a thin sauce leaves the meat wet. Freezes well for up to 3 months; reheat covered until hot through.

recipes.title: Beer-Battered Walleye

groups.name: Fish
ingredients: 1350 g walleye fillets, thawed, skinned, cut crosswise into 14 pieces of about 3 oz
20 g fine salt, for both sides before dredging and right out of the oil (about 3 1/2 tsp)
105 g malt vinegar, to serve (about 7 Tbsp)

steps: Whisk the dry mix ingredients together.
Heat the oil in a deep pot of at least 8 quarts to 190°C, lid on while it climbs and between batches.
Whisk the lager and vodka into the dry mix just to combine, lumps and all. Rest 10 minutes.
Pat the fish dry and salt both sides.
Dredge in flour, shake off, dip in batter and let the excess run.
Lower away from yourself into the 190°C oil.
Fry 3 to 4 minutes, three or four pieces at a time, until the batter is hard and deep gold. Fry the thin tail pieces together.
Drain on a rack and salt immediately.
Serve with malt vinegar, [tartar sauce](tartar-sauce), homemade or jarred, and [chips](triple-cooked-chips).
recipes.notes: The dry mix keeps for days in an airtight container. Cool the oil fully before storing.

nutrition.assumptions: All the batter is counted, with oil absorbed at 12% of the battered fish weight and the beer and vodka ethanol counted in full. The 20 g finishing salt and the malt vinegar are counted; fries and tartar sauce are left out.

changes.note: Fish only now. Fries are just a serve-with.

steps: Cover the bacon lardons with water in a pan, boil the water off, then let them render and crisp in their own fat; drain.

Scramble the eggs soft and slightly underdone.

ingredients: 28 g dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded (about 4)

recipes.title: Chole (Punjabi Chickpea Curry)

ingredients: 250 g dried kabuli chana (chickpeas), soaked overnight (about 1 1/4 cups)
750 g water, for cooking the chickpeas (about 3 cups)
2 g black tea, or a couple dried amla (about 1 tea bag)

groups.name: Masala
ingredients: 3 g black cardamom, lightly cracked (about 2 pods)
6 g anardana (dried pomegranate seed), toasted and ground (about 2 tsp)
3 g amchur (dried green mango powder) (about 1 tsp)
15 g [chole masala](chole-masala), homemade or MDH (about 2 Tbsp)

steps: Soak the chickpeas overnight in plenty of water, then drain.
Pressure-cook the chickpeas with the 750 g fresh water and the tea bag or amla for 35 minutes at high pressure, or simmer covered 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until very soft.
Discard the tea bag and keep the cooking liquid.
Heat 25 g of the ghee in a heavy pan over medium-high and add the black cardamom.
Add the onions and cook, stirring often, until deep golden brown, 15 to 20 minutes.
Add the tomato puree and cook until thick and the ghee separates at the edges, about 10 minutes.
Add the [chole masala](chole-masala), anardana and amchur and stir 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas with about 250 g of their cooking liquid and the salt and MSG.

Crush in the kasuri methi.
Taste and adjust the salt.
Heat the remaining 15 g ghee, fry the ginger and green chili 30 seconds and pour over the chole.
Serve with [spiced basmati rice](spiced-basmati-rice) or plain basmati.

Pour in cold.
Run on the Slush preset.

400 g yellow summer squash, cut into coins (about 2 medium)

recipes.title: Irish Lamb Stew

groups.name: Stew
ingredients: 1.4 kg boneless lamb shoulder, cut in 4 cm pieces
450 g yellow onion, thickly sliced (about 3 medium)
500 g russet potatoes, peeled, cut small (about 2)
1.1 kg red potatoes, peeled, cut in large chunks (about 6 medium)
375 g carrot, cut in chunks (about 6 medium)

groups.name: To finish
ingredients: 1000 g chicken stock, to thin (about 1 L)
700 g sourdough and 100 g salted butter, for serving (about 1 large loaf, 14 slices and 7 Tbsp)

steps: Season the lamb hard with half the salt and half the pepper.
Brown it in lard in batches in a Dutch oven, removing each batch.
Soften the onion in the fat 8 minutes, adding the garlic for the last 2.
Return the lamb and its juices.
Add the stock, russets, bay, thyme, remaining pepper, the rest of the salt and the MSG.
Cover and simmer gently 1 hour.
Add the red potatoes and carrot.
Simmer uncovered 45 minutes, until the lamb is tender and the russets have collapsed into the broth.
Remove the bay leaves, taste and salt again.
Add the Guinness, cover and simmer gently 40 minutes, stirring now and then, so the alcohol cooks off.
Loosen with stock, a splash at a time, until spoonable.
Taste and salt.
Top with parsley and serve with sourdough and butter.
recipes.notes: Sets very thick when cold; thin with stock when reheating. Freezes well for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Kofta (Beef and Lamb Logs)

groups.name: Meat mix
ingredients: 150 g yellow onion, grated and wrung to about 80 g pulp (about 1 medium)
15 to 20 g garlic, grated (about 3 to 4 cloves)

groups.name: To serve
ingredients: 16 [grilled vegetable skewers](grilled-vegetable-skewers), one per wrap (about 2500 g raw vegetables)
2 cups [garlic-dill yogurt sauce](garlic-dill-yogurt-sauce), 2 Tbsp per wrap (about 540 g)
1 1/3 cups [pickled red onions](pickled-red-onions), drained, 20 g per wrap (about 320 g)
4 Charred lemon halves, from 2 lemons (about 200 g)
Sumac and Aleppo pepper for the table (about 1 Tbsp each, 7 g sumac and 6 g Aleppo)

steps: Grate the onion on the fine side of a box grater and wring the pulp hard in a towel.
Combine the beef, lamb, onion pulp, garlic, 20 g spice blend, salt and MSG.
Knead by hand 3 to 5 minutes until the mix is tacky and pulls at your fingers.
Fry a teaspoon-sized test patty and adjust seasoning.
Portion into 16 logs of 2 oz, about 1 inch thick and 4 to 5 inches long, with blunt ends.
Smooth any surface cracks with wet hands.
Chill at least 1 hour.
Double-skewer each cold log on bamboo skewers.
Grill over medium heat 8 to 10 minutes, turning 2 or 3 times, with one burner off as a cool zone for flare-ups.
Pull at 160°F internal.
Warm the pita on the grate 30 seconds a side.
Build each wrap with one log, grilled vegetables, yogurt sauce, pickled onions and a squeeze of charred lemon.

steps: Toast only the cumin and coriander seed in a dry pan over medium heat, 60 to 90 seconds, until fragrant.
Cool completely before grinding.
Grind the cumin, coriander, peppercorns and allspice together.
Crumble in the oregano by hand.
Mix in the paprika, Aleppo, cinnamon and sumac without toasting them.
Jar it.
recipes.notes: Keeps for months in a jar. Salt (15 g kosher) and MSG (2 to 3 g) go into the meat separately, not into the jar. Double for 4 lb of meat. With pre-ground cumin and coriander, use the same weights and skip the toasting.

recipes.title: Louisiana Red Beans and Rice

groups.name: Brine soak
ingredients: 1200 g kidney and pinto beans, sorted and rinsed

groups.name: Pot
ingredients: 700 g andouille sausage, sliced into coins (about two 12 oz packages)
20 g [no-salt Creole seasoning](creole-seasoning), homemade or Tony Chachere's No Salt
1500 g low-sodium chicken stock (about 1 1/2 32 oz cartons)
1500 g water, plus more as needed

groups.name: Finish
ingredients: 94 g kosher salt (to start), plus more to taste

steps: Dissolve the soaking salt in the soaking water, add the beans and soak covered at room temperature 8 to 24 hours.
Drain and rinse the beans.
Heat the lard over medium-high in a stock pot that holds at least 8 quarts.
Brown the andouille in batches and remove to a plate, leaving the fat.
Add the onion, bell pepper and celery; cook over medium, scraping up the fond, until soft, about 10 minutes.
Add the garlic, Creole seasoning, thyme, cayenne and black pepper; stir until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the beans, ham hock, stock, water and bay leaves.
Bring to a full rolling boil and hold it there for at least 10 minutes.
Drop to a low simmer, partially covered, stirring occasionally and scraping the bottom, about 90 minutes, until the beans are fully tender.
Top up with water as needed to keep the beans just covered.
Remove the hock and bay leaves; shred the meat, discard skin and bone and return the meat to the pot with the andouille.
Mash about a third of the beans against the side of the pot (or pulse briefly with an immersion blender).
Simmer uncovered, stirring often, until thick and creamy, about 30 minutes.
Stir in the 94 g salt and the MSG, wait a couple of minutes, then taste a whole bean and add more salt in 5 g hits as needed.
Stir in the hot sauce.
Serve over white rice, topped with the green onion and parsley.
recipes.notes: Freeze without rice, green onion or parsley for up to 3 months; add them fresh when reheating. Thickens a lot when cold; thin with water when reheating and stir often to prevent scorching.

ingredients: 255 g Zatarain's crab boil (about 3 packages, 3 oz each)
1361 g Old Bay (about two 24 oz containers)
340 g kosher salt, only if the water needs it after tasting (about 2 1/2 cups Diamond Crystal)

groups.name: Cook
ingredients: 2700 g small red potatoes (about 6 lb, roughly 50)
1800 g andouille, cut into 1 to 1.5 inch coins on the bias (about 4 lb)
5400 g snow crab clusters, frozen (about 12 lb)
2700 g raw shell-on headless shrimp, 16/20 or 21/25, frozen (about 6 lb)

groups.name: Butter toss
ingredients: ~500 g boil liquor, from the pot (about 500 ml)

steps: Fill a pot of at least 80 quarts, fitted with a basket, with the 10 gallons of water.
Add the Zatarain's, Old Bay, onions, lemons and garlic.
Light the burner; lid on only while bringing the water up from cold. Allow 45 to 60 minutes to a rolling boil.
Boil 5 to 10 minutes, then taste: it should taste like aggressively seasoned soup. Add kosher salt if it does not.
Lid off for the entire cook. Burner on full the entire time.
0:00: add the potatoes and andouille.
Watch for boilover once the potatoes go in; knock the burner down if foam climbs.
0:08: add the corn, mushrooms and frozen crab.
0:16: add the frozen shrimp, or once the pot is back to a full boil, whichever is later.
0:19: ladle out ~500 ml of boil liquor and stir it into the melted garlic Old Bay butter.
Kill the gas. Pull the basket and drain it.
Return the food to the empty, still-hot pot.
Pour the butter and boil liquor over the top, sprinkle the 60 g Old Bay over in two or three passes and toss with the paddle about 10 minutes.
Pour off everything that pools at the bottom into bowls for the table as the dip.
recipes.notes: Melt the butter after any other prep, while the pot climbs. Keep warm until the toss. Hold tiny creamer potatoes until 0:05. Serve on a paper-covered table with [cocktail sauce](cocktail-sauce), [remoulade](remoulade), [serrano ranch](serrano-ranch), [Cajun runoff butter](cajun-runoff-butter) and [drawn lemon butter](drawn-lemon-butter) for dipping. Jarred cocktail sauce, remoulade and ranch work fine.

nutrition.serving: 1 plate, about 830 g edible food with butter (1 of 13)
nutrition.assumptions: Edible yield: crab meat about 25% of cluster weight, shrimp meat about 70% of frozen shell-on weight, about 100 g kernels per ear. Food absorbs about 3% of the boil Old Bay and the full 340 g top-up salt, and the full butter toss (900 g garlic Old Bay butter, 60 g Old Bay, 500 ml liquor) is counted; Zatarain bag spices, the aromatics and table dips are left out.

recipes.title: Rajma (Kidney Bean Curry)

Add the Kashmiri chili powder, coriander, ground cumin and turmeric with a splash of water; stir constantly for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and the 10 g salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until thick and the fat separates at the edges, about 15 minutes.
Remove the cinnamon stick, cardamom pods and cloves from the masala.
Remove the bay leaves from the bean pot.
Scrape the masala into the beans.
Mash about a quarter of the beans against the side of the pot or with an immersion blender.
Simmer uncovered, stirring often, about 30 minutes, until the gravy coats a spoon.
Stir in the garam masala and the kasuri methi crushed between your palms.
Stir in the butter over low heat until emulsified.
Add the 45 g salt and the MSG, tasting a whole bean as you go.

Put them in a pot with the cold water, kosher salt and 30 g malt vinegar.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook until just tender with fuzzy, cracked edges, 8 to 12 minutes from the simmer. Start checking at 6.
Lift out carefully with a spider onto a rack set in a sheet pan.
Let them steam dry 10 minutes, then refrigerate uncovered at least 1 hour, or freeze 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a deep pot of at least 8 quarts to 130°C (265°F).
Parfry in batches 6 to 8 minutes, until a dry, pale skin forms but no color.
Drain on the rack and cool completely, at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oil to 190°C (375°F).
Fry in batches 3 to 5 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on the rack and salt immediately.
Serve with malt vinegar.
recipes.notes: The parfried chips keep up to 2 days refrigerated, or freeze in a single layer, then bag; fry from frozen. Beef dripping is the traditional frying fat.

nutrition.assumptions: Oil absorbed at about 9% of cooked weight; about 5% of the parboiling salt and all 15 g of finishing salt counted; malt vinegar counted.

recipes.title: Vinegar Slaw

ingredients: 600 g green cabbage, shredded (about 1/2 medium head)
3 g black pepper, freshly ground (about 1 1/2 tsp)

steps: Whisk the vinegar, sugar, oil, salt, celery seed and pepper.
Pour over the cabbage and carrot and toss.
Refrigerate.
recipes.notes: Improves over a few days refrigerated; goes limp by 5 days.
